  • Constructor Details

    • SemenovSelfHeatingResult

      public SemenovSelfHeatingResult(double volumeM3, double surfaceAreaM2, double heatTransferCoefficientWPerM2K, double activationEnergyJPerMol, double volumetricPreFactorWPerM3, double ambientTemperatureK, double psi, double psiCrit, double psiRatio, double criticalTemperatureK, double temperatureMarginK, double criticalTemperatureRiseK, SelfHeatingVerdict verdict, List<String> warnings)
      Construct a Semenov self-heating result.
      Parameters:
      volumeM3 - reacting volume in m3
      surfaceAreaM2 - heat-loss surface area in m2
      heatTransferCoefficientWPerM2K - external heat-transfer coefficient in W/(m2 K)
      activationEnergyJPerMol - apparent activation energy in J/mol
      volumetricPreFactorWPerM3 - volumetric heat-release pre-exponential factor in W/m3
      ambientTemperatureK - ambient temperature in K
      psi - the Semenov criticality parameter, dimensionless
      psiCrit - the critical Semenov parameter (1/e), dimensionless
      psiRatio - ratio psi / psiCrit, dimensionless
      criticalTemperatureK - critical ambient temperature in K, NaN if not bracketed
      temperatureMarginK - critical temperature minus ambient temperature in K, positive when safe
      criticalTemperatureRiseK - steady self-heating excess at criticality R*Ta^2/E in K
      verdict - the screening verdict
      warnings - list of warnings; may be null

      public double getPsiRatio()
      Gets the ratio of the Semenov parameter to its critical value. Values above 1 indicate that no steady state exists.
      Returns:

    • getTemperatureMarginK

      public double getTemperatureMarginK()

      Returns:
      temperature margin in K, positive when subcritical, or NaN if the critical temperature is unknown

    • getCriticalTemperatureRiseK

      public double getCriticalTemperatureRiseK()
      Gets the steady self-heating temperature excess at criticality, R * Ta^2 / E. This is how much hotter than its surroundings the body runs at the point of criticality, and is typically small enough to escape notice.
      Returns:
      critical temperature rise in K
